en.p: As shown in the figure, in the quadrilateral ABCD with

the two triangles ABC and ACD are both acute triangles. Let E be the point dividing segment AC internally in the ratio $1:2$. Let $\mathrm{P_1}$, $\mathrm{P_2}$ be the points other than A where the circle with diameter AE meets the segments AB and AD, respectively, and let $\mathrm{Q_1}$, $\mathrm{Q_2}$ be the points other than C where the circle with diameter CE meets the segments BC and CD, respectively.

When $\overline{\mathrm{P_1P_2}}:\overline{\mathrm{Q_1Q_2}}=3:5\sqrt{2}$ and the area of triangle ABD is 2, what is the value of $\overline{\mathrm{AB}}+\overline{\mathrm{AD}}$? (Here $\overline{\mathrm{AB}}>\overline{\mathrm{AD}}$.) [4 points]
